full_judgment: 4. Plaintiff having died during continuation of the suit, she was substituted by order No. 113 dated 29-3-1995. Substituted Plaintiffs thereafter filed an application for amendment of the plaint wherein it has been stated that Bhogaban Chandra Deb was possessing schedules 1 and 2 of the suit land, gave settlement of the said land to Kunjanath Bhattacharya, Provashani Dey, Soudamini Dey, Borda Kanta, Aboni Kanta Roy, Bonkim Chandra Dey, Ramesh Chandra Dey, Armada Charan Dey and Kanaklata Debi and realized rents from them and was in successive possession of schedule 3 land. In the said situation, said Bhogaban Chandra Deb transferred by a deed of gift, 52 decimals of land on 21-8-48 to Kantibhushan Deb, Narayan Chandra Deb, Shib Prashad Deb and 44 decimals of land of schedule 3 land by a deed of gift dated 21-8-1948 to Shanty Bhushan Deb, Tikendra Kumer Deb and Promod Kumer Deb and 75 decimals of land, which is situated north of the pond, to his six grand-sons, that is, Shanti Bhushan Deb, Tikendra Kumer Deb, Promod Kumer Deb, Karitibhushan Deb, Narayan Chandra Deb and Shib Prashad Deb and they were in possession of those land. Bhogaban Chandra Deb by another deed of gift on 23-8-48 transferred 31/2 decimals of land from dag No 281 with structures to defendant No. 3, Khitesh Chandra Deb and by another deed of gift, being No. 6827 of the year 1950, transferred 314 decimal of land from dag No. 282 to his daughter, Manda Sundari and delivered possession. Bhogaban Chandra Deb retains the superior interest for 1.78 decimals of land of schedule 3 and thereafter died. By a Kabala-dated 5-4-54, Suresh Chandra Deb and his 3 sons, transferred 811/2 decimals of land from schedule No. 3 to the plaintiff and delivered possession and since then the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land and SA Khatian No. 557 was correctly prepared in her name in respect of 811/2 decimals of land and was finally published. Shanti Bhushan Deb and his other two brothers, who got schedule 2 land from their father Bhogaban Chandra Deb and on his death, these three brothers got schedule 3 lands by inheritance and on amicable settlement, Shanti Bhushan Deb got 3 (ka) schedule land and his two brothers in exchange, got the lands of India. Khitesh Chandra Deb, who got 31/2 decimals of land from dag No. 281 and Manda Sundari got 3112 decimals of land from dag No. 281, by kabala deed dated 27-11-56 and 12-2-57, sold the said land to Abu Mohammad Shahnawaz, son of the plaintiff, who became the owner and possessor of the said land. After became title-less, Khitesh Chandra having fell in helpless condition, approach the plaintiff who gave him permission to possess dag No. 1925 and in such situation, Khitesh Chandra Deb wrongly recorded his name in SA Khatian. Khitesh Chandra Deb had/have no title, interest or possession in respect of said dag. Shanti Bhushan Deb through bainapatra dated 18-9-58 transferred schedule 3Ka land to the plaintiff and delivered khas possession, which includes the property requisitioned by the Government. The plaintiff by dint of said bainapatra, is in possession of half of the ponds situated in dag No. 281. Item Nos. 1, 2, 3 and schedule 3(ka) having been requisitioned by the Government, as such, the tenants of the Government are possessing the said land. The said property having been de-requisitioned and the plaintiff having been purchased the said lands and having been in possession and title over the said lands, the plaintiff acquired title of his predecessor in those lands. During SA operation, the name of Shanti Bhushan was recorded in SA Khatian No. 554 and the plaintiff having been purchased the said land from Shanti Bhushan and by paying rents, is in possession of the said land, thereby acquired good title over the suit land.
